key_insight: A differentiable, GPU-accelerated acoustic simulator can infer vocal tract shape from speech by optimizing a geometry model to match the sounds it produces.
clinical_relevance: This could support noninvasive speech and airway-related imaging workflows by reconstructing moving vocal tract geometry from audio, potentially reducing reliance on paired MRI data.
method: Built a frequency-domain acoustic tube simulator that is far more GPU-parallelizable than time-domain finite differences.
Added a differentiable turbulence model to capture consonant sounds.
Used neural-network geometry parameterization to improve optimization and avoid local minima.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports self-supervised autoencoding across 11 languages and a speech-to-moving-vocal-tract reconstruction pipeline coupled with MRI generation, but it does not provide quantitative results here.
watch_item: Inverse reconstruction is still non-convex and may be sensitive to optimization quality, language coverage, and the realism of the simulator assumptions.
paper_title: Reconstructing the Vocal Tract with Differentiable Acoustic Simulation
